en: The Analysis of the Bhikkhunī Rules,
2.4 Section on Compendium (Saṅgahavāra) For a lustful bhikkhunī who consents to physical contact with a lustful person, how many of the seven classes of offenses do those offenses fall under?
For a lustful bhikkhunī who consents to physical contact with a lustful person, those offenses are comprised within three of the seven classes of offenses.

They may be included in the class of offenses involving defeat (pārājika), they may be included in the class of grave offenses (thullaccaya), or they may be included in the class of offenses of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) … [and so on] … How many of the seven classes of offenses do the offenses of one who asks for curd and eats it comprise?
The offenses of one who asks for curd and eats it are comprised within two of the seven classes of offenses: [namely, the class of grave offenses and the class of offenses of wrong-doing].
It may be by way of the class of offenses entailing confession (pāṭidesanīya), or it may be by way of the class of offenses of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
The fourth section on inclusion is finished.
